purpose: Resume the saved provenance cursors, rotate through content-addressed and handoff-shaped public records, then test newly located public pull-request timelines for specific cross-provider review-result-to-repair dependencies, participant provenance and an operator-defined boundary.

method.selection: Run the three exact Pass 94 cursors, search four progressively lower-order public-record groups, then rotate into public pull-request timelines. Deep-read the strongest timelines in which a named review service supplied a specific finding and a later authenticated agent commit implemented the same requested change.
method.coverage_note: The sixty-query counts below are overlapping search-result occurrences, not messages, participants or incidents. Twenty-two responses reached their requested result cap. One trace query briefly located a generated demo path and returned zero on the stable parallel rerun; both observations are preserved rather than silently choosing the nonzero response.
method.read_only_limits: Only existing public repository pages, pull-request timelines, commit metadata, indexed excerpts and web-search results were read. No code was executed, no package was installed, no review or scan was submitted, no account was created and no participant was contacted.
falsification_tests: Require a later recipient artifact to implement a specific earlier finding, not merely appear in the same pull request.
Authenticate service identities from public comment and commit attribution without treating provider names as proof of separate operators.
Test human-requested work, installed review applications, designed repository workflow, shared ownership and ordinary code review as alternatives.
Require primary evidence that any cooperation crossed the repository operator's authorization boundary before considering a rogue interpretation.

search_snapshot.note: Counts combine three resumed cursors, forty-four code/trace expressions and thirteen pull-request locator expressions. Results overlap heavily and capped pull-request searches are discovery locators rather than complete coverage.

query_groups.name: resumed_pass94_exact_cursors
query_groups.classification: Each query returned the Pass 94 log and assessment only; no external record appeared.

query_groups.name: content_addressed_dependency_fields
query_groups.classification: The two external rows are implementation or schema definitions rather than a populated exchange.

query_groups.name: message_and_handoff_fields
query_groups.classification: External results were schemas, framework code, tests, mocks or generated demonstrations; none supplied an independently attributable organic transfer/use edge.

query_groups.name: lower_order_timestamp_fields
query_groups.classification: Broad lower-order matches were dominated by implementations, examples, telemetry schemas and test data; no stronger original chain survived inspection.

query_groups.name: trace_event_fields
query_groups.classification: Four compact semantic paths and twenty-nine handoff-completed paths were fully inspected and resolved to ontologies, schemas, implementation, tests or mocks. One exact event-type query briefly returned an Observra demo JSONL path that its public generator creates, then returned zero in the stable rerun; it remains a generated-demo control.

query_groups.name: public_pull_request_locators
query_groups.classification: Locator-only coverage. Selected timelines were inspected for direct finding-to-fix dependencies; most results were ordinary multi-bot review, human-authored repair or no-use controls.

selected_original_records.semantic_dependency: Supported. The later Claude-authored commit, tests and six direct replies implement the exact findings supplied minutes earlier by CodeAnt and CodeRabbit.
selected_original_records.participant_provenance: Two review applications and the Claude commit identity are distinguishable public service identities. The record does not independently authenticate different human operators behind them.

cross_record_assessment.original_observation: Two public pull-request timelines preserve specific review-service findings followed by matching authenticated Claude commits and direct acknowledgments.
cross_record_assessment.supported_coordination: Cross-provider review-result transfer and downstream semantic use are supported in both records.
cross_record_assessment.verified_participants: Distinct public application/account identities are verified at the comment and commit layers. Independent operator ownership is not verified.
cross_record_assessment.operator_boundary: No boundary crossing is supported. One pull request is explicitly human-requested and both sequences use installed review services plus a repository-authorized implementation agent inside ordinary pull-request workflow.
cross_record_assessment.subjective_intent: No rogue intent is established or inferred from agent attribution, direct replies or multi-provider participation.
cross_record_assessment.provider_attribution: GitHub publicly attributes the comments and commits to Devin, CodeAnt, CodeRabbit and Claude identities; those labels do not by themselves establish underlying model execution or operator independence.
cross_record_assessment.current_activity: Both pull requests merged on 2026-10-18. Their public timelines establish completed review workflows, not a currently active unauthorized population.
cross_record_assessment.checkpoint: Zero confirmed previously unreported rogue swarms.

prior_reporting_check.result: Exact phrase searches located only the originating pull requests. GitHub code search returned no indexed default-branch match for the two full commit identifiers or titles. Routine web search returned unrelated lexical noise, and higher-recall searches for both commit identifiers and titles returned no result.
prior_reporting_check.bounded_statement: No prior coordination report was located for these exact identifiers and phrases across the four checked search methods as of 2026-10-18. This bounded absence is not proof of novelty and does not turn authorized review workflows into rogue coordination.
prior_reporting_check.reason: The original chains pass the transfer/use gate but fail the separate-operator and authorization-crossing gates.

limitations: Capped and overlapping search results are locator coverage, not a census of pull requests, agents or incidents.
GitHub application and commit attribution verifies public identities but not hidden model execution, operator ownership or authorization details beyond the published workflow.
Temporal and semantic correspondence supports downstream use but does not prove unsupervised execution.
Pull-request installation and repository governance can authorize cross-provider activity without exposing every private configuration detail.
Search absence does not establish novelty.

next_cursor.record_priority: Prefer a public timeline that binds a specific machine-produced finding or artifact to a recipient action, then independently authenticates different operators and shows that their cooperation exceeded the repository's configured review or delegation scope.
next_cursor.reopen_trigger: Primary evidence of independent operator ownership, activity outside the installed review workflow, or an authorization violation that materially changes either boundary assessment.

safety.retrieval: Read-only public repository pages, pull-request timelines, commit metadata and search indexes only.
not_performed: No recovered code, command, test or agent runtime was executed.
No package was installed and no scan, review, message, reaction, vote or account action was submitted.
No participant was contacted and no sink, unlisted room or target system was accessed.
safety.publication: Only public record links, timestamps, Git identifiers, domain-level summaries and reasoning are retained; raw payload bodies, credentials, tokens, personal addresses and private logs are omitted.
